From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law

## Overall Assessment

The Seller describes its package as "fair and balanced." It isn't. Three structural moves combine to make the warranties close to worthless:

1. **One liability regime for everything** (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5), including title, fraud and specific indemnities.
2. **General disclosure of the whole data room** (DL 1.1–1.2).
3. **A constructive-knowledge bar** (Clause 8.3).

Together these mean almost every known risk (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) is disclosed away, capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred at 18 months. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts several "settled" statements in its cover note. Items 2–6 show that Bluefen and Riverlark are not resolved, the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow, and the incident is unassessed.

The figures below are opening negotiation positions. Calibrate them against any W&I insurance strategy and the final due diligence record.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (Cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap on general Warranty Claims of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A general cap of 30–40% of price (AUD 7.2m–9.6m). The cap must apply only to general warranties. Title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities and leakage should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted and counter at 35%, with an express carve-out list.
- **Reason:** 20% is at the low end of the market, and with no category carve-outs it would cap known, quantified risks that already exceed AUD 4.8m.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (Cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Deductible basket of AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated. A **tipping** basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%), so the full amount is recoverable once it is crossed. Neither threshold should apply to title, tax, indemnities or leakage.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket at 0.5%, a lower de minimis, and an aggregation rule for related claims.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket above 1% means the Buyer silently absorbs the first AUD 250k of every loss scenario. The three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110k each show how easily related items fall under a per-claim de minimis if they are not aggregated.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (Cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so the window covers two full audit cycles. Separate, longer periods should apply to other categories (see SPA-N-004, N-014 and N-016). The default rule should be reversed: limitations apply only to the categories expressly named.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 18–24 months for general warranties only, and reject the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** The default rule quietly imports the 18-month bar into title, tax and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties take the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Cap at 100% of price (AUD 24m).
  - Survival for the full statutory limitation period: 6 years in contract under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW), or 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - Not qualified by disclosure or knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. A 20% cap on that warranty is not a simplification. It removes the core bargain.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out disapplying all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for:
  - fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers; and
  - claims under the Australian Consumer Law, including s 18, to the extent they cannot lawfully be excluded.

  Fraud of the Company's management known to the Seller should be captured as well.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on this. It is a non-negotiable drafting point.
- **Reason:** Exclusion of liability for one's own fraud is likely unenforceable in any event. Leaving it unstated invites argument and signals intent, and the "any nature" wording would otherwise cap and time-bar fraud claims.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** Disclosure of the whole indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only **specific** disclosures in the Disclosure Letter count, and each must be fair, meaning sufficient detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public records, beyond possibly a narrow list of named searches.
  - Disclosure does not qualify title/capacity warranties, tax warranties, specific indemnities or leakage.
  - A bring-down Disclosure Letter at Completion, which itself does not cure breaches arising between signing and Completion and gives the Buyer a walk right for material matters.
- **Recommendation:** Strike DL 1.1–1.2 and adopt a specific, fair-disclosure standard.
- **Reason:** The disclosure date is already six weeks stale (22 Sept vs today, 5 Nov 2026), and data-room-wide disclosure lets the Seller rely on documents it never flagged.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (Cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge or investigation. As a fallback, the bar applies only to matters Fairly Disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and never to indemnities, title or tax.
- **Recommendation:** Delete Clause 8.3 and replace it with a pro-sandbagging clause.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge, including advisers' knowledge, turns the Buyer's diligence into a waiver and duplicates the general data-room disclosure.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (Cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:** "Addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's **unconditional** written change-of-control consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, all in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The condition is waivable only by the Buyer, and the Seller is held to an "all reasonable endeavours" standard.
  - No adverse amendment to the Bluefen contract as the price of consent.
  - A Buyer termination right at the sunset date.
  - A fallback price adjustment or earn-out on Bluefen revenue if the Buyer elects to waive.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "addressed." Make this a hard, Buyer-only CP.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. DL item 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met, and consent "on delivery" alone ignores those conditions.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (Cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD ~3.2m outstanding (plus accrued interest and break costs) treated as Indebtedness and deducted from the price, paid directly to Riverlark at Completion under a signed payoff letter.
  - At Completion, delivery of a deed of release, PPSR (Personal Property Securities Register) financing statement discharges, and release of any share or guarantee security. This is a Completion deliverable, not a post-Completion promise.
  - A waiver, or confirmation that no default is triggered, under DD-003 cl 8.1, the change-control clause.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Payoff and discharge must happen simultaneously at Completion.
- **Reason:** The debt-free price assumes this debt is gone. DL item 3 confirms it is unpaid and undischarged, and the cl 8.1 change of control may trigger default or acceleration the moment the shares transfer.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD 420k plus all on-costs (employer superannuation, NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation, and any PAYG withholding the Company must remit) defined as Transaction Expenses/Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through the Company's payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later on-cost assessment, outside the cap and thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Require this to be itemised in the funds flow, with an indemnity.
- **Reason:** The employer is the Company, so a liability "for the Seller" off the funds flow lands on the Buyer post-Completion. DL item 5 admits the on-costs are unaddressed.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (Cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Completion deliverables:** Bank-verified evidence that every SOW3 fee is cleared (DD-010 shows AUD 180k open), and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials and IP under DD-004 cl 7.3.
  - **Indemnity:** A standalone indemnity covering all loss from any failure of the Company to own or freely use the SOW3 materials. This includes infringement claims, re-development and replacement costs, and business interruption. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, survive at least 6 years, and be supported by a retention or escrow.
  - **Status:** Make this a CP if the IP is core to the product.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Require an assignment at Completion plus a broad indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3 title does not pass until every fee clears. Paying AUD 180k does not fix past non-ownership or third-party claims, and the Seller concedes there is no payment receipt or assignment (DL item 4).

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006, Cl 4.6/Sch 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** The Seller causes the Company to complete an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* (Cth)), make any required OAIC and individual notifications, attempt recall or deletion of the link, and share all findings with the Buyer.
  - **Specific indemnity:** Covers regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and remediation. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, survive at least 4–6 years, and be backed by a retention.
  - **Warranty:** No other incidents.
  - **Insurance:** Confirm cyber insurance has been notified.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not material." Require a specific indemnity plus a remediation covenant.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records went to an unintended external recipient, and as at 22 September access, scope and notifiability were all undetermined. The Act's 30-day assessment expectation may already have lapsed, which adds compliance exposure the Seller is pricing at zero.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of the three renewals and an explanation of their timing, scope and whether they are terminable.
  - Confirmation of whether the split into three AUD 110k tranches avoided any approval or delegation threshold.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that ban new or renewed contracts above a threshold without Buyer consent.
  - Aggregation of related claims.
  - Where a renewal is non-ordinary-course or not for the Company's benefit: treatment as Leakage or a price adjustment, or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation. Verify first, then treat as Leakage or adjust price where unjustified.
- **Reason:** DL item 8 itself says the renewals must be "read together" and makes no ordinary-course statement. Three identical related renewals together exceed the proposed AUD 250k basket while each sits under per-claim thresholds.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: one cap, one threshold set and one time limit for "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct, separately defined categories, each with its own rules:

  | Category | Cap | Thresholds | Survival | Disclosure/knowledge |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | General warranties | ~35% | Apply | 24 months | Specific disclosure only |
  | Title/capacity | 100% | None | Statutory | Not qualified |
  | Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | None | 7 years | Not qualified |
  | Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar) | 100% or tailored | None | Tailored | Not qualified |
  | Leakage / price adjustment | Dollar-for-dollar | None | Not subject to warranty limitations | Not qualified |
  | Fraud | Unlimited | None | Unlimited | Not qualified |

  Retention or escrow should secure the indemnity categories.
- **Recommendation:** Rebuild the limitations schedule around these categories.
- **Reason:** Category separation is the mechanism that stops N-001 to N-003 from swallowing title, tax and the known specific risks.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Buyer's own verification:** ASIC current and historical company extracts; reconciliation of the register against all share issue and transfer documents and the constitution; PPSR and ASIC charges searches.
  - **Confirmations:** No options, convertibles, employee share or option schemes, or pre-emption rights.
  - **Warranty:** A full fundamental title warranty: legal and beneficial ownership of 100%, fully paid, free of Encumbrances.
  - **Completion deliverables:** Signed share transfers, share certificates, board approval of registration, waivers of pre-emption rights, and release of any Riverlark share security.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Make title a fundamental warranty and complete the verification steps.
- **Reason:** A register is evidence of title, not proof of it. DL item 10 expressly disclaims Buyer verification, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime," meaning the 20% cap, the AUD 250k basket, 18 months, and qualification by disclosure and knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including tax on the bonuses and Completion payments, at a 100% cap with no thresholds. Survival of about 7 years, or until the relevant ATO amendment period expires plus a buffer (unlimited for fraud or evasion), not qualified by disclosure. Conduct-of-claims provisions are acceptable.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, contractor and employee assignments, open-source compliance, data/privacy) with a 3–4 year survival, plus the Ironquay-specific indemnity in N-011.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open terms, not settled, and table full drafting.
- **Reason:** ATO assessment windows run years past 18 months. The Ironquay and DD-006 facts show live IP and data risk, so neither can sit in the general basket.

---

## Additional Points for the Mark-up
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says no consent is triggered by the share sale. Have counsel confirm this against the actual clauses, including any change-of-control-as-deemed-assignment wording. Make any required notifications Completion deliverables.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable only if paired with an express statement that it does not limit the Buyer's indemnity or warranty rights.
- **Leakage and conduct-of-business covenants:** Add a locked-box or completion-accounts protection covering the period between signing and Completion, given the Sandbar renewals and bonuses.
- **Stale disclosure date:** Require an updated data-room index and Disclosure Letter as at signing, with a bring-down at Completion.
- **W&I insurance:** If proposed, it will likely exclude the known matters (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), so those *must* be covered by specific Seller indemnities and retention.

Should I turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 13 and the Disclosure Letter, or into an issues list in the Buyer's standard negotiation table format?

- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge, including advisers' knowledge, turns the Buyer's diligence into a waiver and duplicates the general data-room disclosure.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (Cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:** "Addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's **unconditional** written change-of-control consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, all in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - The condition is waivable only by the Buyer, and the Seller is held to an "all reasonable endeavours" standard.
  - No adverse amendment to the Bluefen contract as the price of consent.
  - A Buyer termination right at the sunset date.
  - A fallback price adjustment or earn-out on Bluefen revenue if the Buyer elects to waive.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "addressed." Make this a hard, Buyer-only CP.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. DL item 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met, and consent "on delivery" alone ignores those conditions.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (Cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD ~3.2m outstanding (plus accrued interest and break costs) treated as Indebtedness and deducted from the price, paid directly to Riverlark at Completion under a signed payoff letter.
  - At Completion, delivery of a deed of release, PPSR (Personal Property Securities Register) financing statement discharges, and release of any share or guarantee security. This is a Completion deliverable, not a post-Completion promise.
  - A waiver, or confirmation that no default is triggered, under DD-003 cl 8.1, the change-control clause.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Payoff and discharge must happen simultaneously at Completion.
- **Reason:** The debt-free price assumes this debt is gone. DL item 3 confirms it is unpaid and undischarged, and the cl 8.1 change of control may trigger default or acceleration the moment the shares transfer.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD 420k plus all on-costs (employer superannuation, NSW payroll tax, workers' compensation, and any PAYG withholding the Company must remit) defined as Transaction Expenses/Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through the Company's payroll at Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later on-cost assessment, outside the cap and thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Require this to be itemised in the funds flow, with an indemnity.
- **Reason:** The employer is the Company, so a liability "for the Seller" off the funds flow lands on the Buyer post-Completion. DL item 5 admits the on-costs are unaddressed.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (Cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Completion deliverables:** Bank-verified evidence that every SOW3 fee is cleared (DD-010 shows AUD 180k open), and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials and IP under DD-004 cl 7.3.
  - **Indemnity:** A standalone indemnity covering all loss from any failure of the Company to own or freely use the SOW3 materials. This includes infringement claims, re-development and replacement costs, and business interruption. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, survive at least 6 years, and be supported by a retention or escrow.
  - **Status:** Make this a CP if the IP is core to the product.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Require an assignment at Completion plus a broad indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3 title does not pass until every fee clears. Paying AUD 180k does not fix past non-ownership or third-party claims, and the Seller concedes there is no payment receipt or assignment (DL item 4).

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006, Cl 4.6/Sch 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** The Seller causes the Company to complete an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* (Cth)), make any required OAIC and individual notifications, attempt recall or deletion of the link, and share all findings with the Buyer.
  - **Specific indemnity:** Covers regulatory penalties, investigation and notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and remediation. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, survive at least 4–6 years, and be backed by a retention.
  - **Warranty:** No other incidents.
  - **Insurance:** Confirm cyber insurance has been notified.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not material." Require a specific indemnity plus a remediation covenant.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records went to an unintended external recipient, and as at 22 September access, scope and notifiability were all undetermined. The Act's 30-day assessment expectation may already have lapsed, which adds compliance exposure the Seller is pricing at zero.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of the three renewals and an explanation of their timing, scope and whether they are terminable.
  - Confirmation of whether the split into three AUD 110k tranches avoided any approval or delegation threshold.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that ban new or renewed contracts above a threshold without Buyer consent.
  - Aggregation of related claims.
  - Where a renewal is non-ordinary-course or not for the Company's benefit: treatment as Leakage or a price adjustment, or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation. Verify first, then treat as Leakage or adjust price where unjustified.
- **Reason:** DL item 8 itself says the renewals must be "read together" and makes no ordinary-course statement. Three identical related renewals together exceed the proposed AUD 250k basket while each sits under per-claim thresholds.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: one cap, one threshold set and one time limit for "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct, separately defined categories, each with its own rules:

  | Category | Cap | Thresholds | Survival | Disclosure/knowledge |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | General warranties | ~35% | Apply | 24 months | Specific disclosure only |
  | Title/capacity | 100% | None | Statutory | Not qualified |
  | Tax warranties and indemnity | 100% | None | 7 years | Not qualified |
  | Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar) | 100% or tailored | None | Tailored | Not qualified |
  | Leakage / price adjustment | Dollar-for-dollar | None | Not subject to warranty limitations | Not qualified |
  | Fraud | Unlimited | None | Unlimited | Not qualified |

  Retention or escrow should secure the indemnity categories.
- **Recommendation:** Rebuild the limitations schedule around these categories.
- **Reason:** Category separation is the mechanism that stops N-001 to N-003 from swallowing title, tax and the known specific risks.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Buyer's own verification:** ASIC current and historical company extracts; reconciliation of the register against all share issue and transfer documents and the constitution; PPSR and ASIC charges searches.
  - **Confirmations:** No options, convertibles, employee share or option schemes, or pre-emption rights.
  - **Warranty:** A full fundamental title warranty: legal and beneficial ownership of 100%, fully paid, free of Encumbrances.
  - **Completion deliverables:** Signed share transfers, share certificates, board approval of registration, waivers of pre-emption rights, and release of any Riverlark share security.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Make title a fundamental warranty and complete the verification steps.
- **Reason:** A register is evidence of title, not proof of it. DL item 10 expressly disclaims Buyer verification, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime," meaning the 20% cap, the AUD 250k basket, 18 months, and qualification by disclosure and knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including tax on the bonuses and Completion payments, at a 100% cap with no thresholds. Survival of about 7 years, or until the relevant ATO amendment period expires plus a buffer (unlimited for fraud or evasion), not qualified by disclosure. Conduct-of-claims provisions are acceptable.
  - **IP:** Full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, contractor and employee assignments, open-source compliance, data/privacy) with a 3–4 year survival, plus the Ironquay-specific indemnity in N-011.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open terms, not settled, and table full drafting.
- **Reason:** ATO assessment windows run years past 18 months. The Ironquay and DD-006 facts show live IP and data risk, so neither can sit in the general basket.
